definition: Assigning a class label to a detected or cropped object — the fundamental building block of image recognition.
details: Assigning a class label to a detected or cropped object — the fundamental building block of image recognition.

explainer.lead: Object classification turns a detected or cropped object into a named class. It matters because it is the building block on which image recognition systems are assembled.

tiers.eli5: Like picking up a photo of one thing, such as a chair, and deciding what it is; other steps do the picking out, and this step does the naming.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers feed crops from a detector into a classifier, or attach a classification head to the detector, and a common pitfall is classifying poorly framed crops whose object is cut off.
tiers.paperLevel: A mapping from an image region to one label from a fixed set of classes, learned from labelled examples; it assumes the object is already isolated, so it gives no position.

explainer.example: A crop around a parked vehicle is passed in and the model outputs 'car' with a probability.
